title: Phase Shift and Midline
short: y = A sin(B(x − h)) + k shifts by h and centers on y = k.
trouble: Students read the shift of sin(2x − π) as π instead of π/2.

blocks.html: Two more transformations complete the picture: sliding the wave sideways and lifting it up or down. They work the same way as shifts of any graph, with one catch when $B \ne 1$.

In $$\role{output}{y} = \role[amplitude]{coefficient}{A}\sin\big(\role[frequency factor]{frequency}{B}(\role{input}{x} - \role[horizontal shift]{shift}{h})\big) + \role{midline}{k},$$ the graph shifts right by $h$ (left if $h < 0$), and the midline is $y = k$. The maximum is $k + |A|$ and the minimum is $k - |A|$. If the equation is written $y = A\sin(Bx - C) + k$, factor out $B$ first: the shift is $h = \frac{C}{B}$.

The basic wave starts a cycle where its input is $0$. Here the input is $B(x - h)$, which is $0$ when $x = h$. So the cycle that used to start at $0$ now starts at $h$. Adding $k$ raises every point by $k$, so the center line moves from $y = 0$ to $y = k$, and the wave still swings $|A|$ above and below it.

opts.task: Build $y = \sin(2x - \pi)$: set $B = 2$ and find the shift that matches.

blocks.cap: The gold dot marks where a cycle starts. The readout warns when the shift is not the number you see inside the parentheses.

blocks.title: All the features
steps: $h = \frac{\pi}{4}$: shifted right $\frac{\pi}{4}$. $B = 1$, so the period is $2\pi$.

blocks.title: Factor first
steps: Check: the inside is $0$ when $2x + \frac{\pi}{3} = 0$, that is $x = -\frac{\pi}{6}$. ✓

blocks.title: Building an equation
blocks.q: Write a sine function with amplitude $2$, period $\pi$, a shift of $\frac{\pi}{4}$ to the right and midline $y = -1$.

blocks.html: Reading the shift of $\sin(2x - \pi)$ as $\pi$. The number inside is $C = Bh$, not $h$. Quick check: set the inside equal to $0$ and solve. $2x - \pi = 0$ gives $x = \frac{\pi}{2}$, so the shift is $\frac{\pi}{2}$.
